theory.intro: A dot plot or an ordered stem-and-leaf plot shows the data in order, so you can read the five-number summary from the display. Check that the stems and leaves are ordered before applying the procedure; order them first if needed. The five-number summary is the minimum, $Q_1$, $Q_2$, $Q_3$ and maximum, in that order.
facts: Once the data is in order, $Q_1$ is the median of the lower half and $Q_3$ the median of the upper half.
Exclude the median itself from both halves when $n$ is odd.
The minimum is the first value shown — the leftmost dot, or the smallest stem's first leaf — and the maximum is the last.
steps: Read the data from the display, in ascending order
Find $Q_1$, the median of the lower half
Find $Q_3$, the median of the upper half

workedExamples.solution_text:
Count every dot, including repeated scores. The ordered data is:

$2,\ 4,\ 4,\ 6,\ 8,\ 8,\ 8,\ 10,\ 14$.

There are $9$ scores, so $Q_2$ is the fifth score: $Q_2=8$.

Exclude that fifth score when forming the halves. The lower half is $2,\ 4,\ 4,\ 6$; the upper half is $8,\ 8,\ 10,\ 14$.

$\begin{align*}Q_1&=\frac{4+4}{2}\\&=4\end{align*}$

$\begin{align*}Q_3&=\frac{8+10}{2}\\&=9\end{align*}$

The leftmost dot gives the minimum, $2$, and the rightmost dot gives the maximum, $14$.

Five-number summary: $2,\ 4,\ 8,\ 9,\ 14$.

Reading every dot from left to right gives:

$1,\ 3,\ 3,\ 5,\ 7,\ 7,\ 9,\ 11$.

There are $8$ scores. Average the fourth and fifth scores to find the median.

$\begin{align*}Q_2&=\frac{5+7}{2}\\&=6\end{align*}$

Split the data into two halves of four scores: $1,\ 3,\ 3,\ 5$ and $7,\ 7,\ 9,\ 11$.

$\begin{align*}Q_1&=\frac{3+3}{2}\\&=3\end{align*}$

$\begin{align*}Q_3&=\frac{7+9}{2}\\&=8\end{align*}$

The minimum is $1$ and the maximum is $11$.

Five-number summary: $1,\ 3,\ 6,\ 8,\ 11$.

Use the key to combine each stem and leaf. The empty stem $11$ contributes no values.

The ordered data is:

$102,\ 104,\ 108,\ 109,\ 122,\ 125,\ 128,\ 131,\ 139$.

There are $9$ values, so the fifth value is the median: $Q_2=122$.

Exclude this value. The lower half is $102,\ 104,\ 108,\ 109$; the upper half is $125,\ 128,\ 131,\ 139$.

$\begin{align*}Q_1&=\frac{104+108}{2}\\&=106\end{align*}$

$\begin{align*}Q_3&=\frac{128+131}{2}\\&=129.5\end{align*}$

The first value is $102$ and the last value is $139$.

Five-number summary: $102,\ 106,\ 122,\ 129.5,\ 139$.

Read the stems and leaves in order:

$22,\ 27,\ 31,\ 34,\ 38,\ 42,\ 46,\ 49,\ 53,\ 58,\ 60,\ 64$.

There are $12$ values. Average the sixth and seventh values to find the median.

$\begin{align*}Q_2&=\frac{42+46}{2}\\&=44\end{align*}$

The lower six values are $22,\ 27,\ 31,\ 34,\ 38,\ 42$. Average their third and fourth values.

$\begin{align*}Q_1&=\frac{31+34}{2}\\&=32.5\end{align*}$

The upper six values are $46,\ 49,\ 53,\ 58,\ 60,\ 64$. Average their third and fourth values.

$\begin{align*}Q_3&=\frac{53+58}{2}\\&=55.5\end{align*}$

The minimum is $22$ and the maximum is $64$.

Five-number summary: $22,\ 32.5,\ 44,\ 55.5,\ 64$.
